title: Grateful Dead Live at Alfred College on 1970-05-01
lineage: CD -> Adobe Audition v1.5 ->Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC
source: Source 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD Source 2: SBD ->Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD Source 3: SBD -> Master Reel -> Reel-> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard capture of the May 1 1970 Alfred show – crystal‑clear acoustic set plus a scorching electric half, despite minor low‑end mud and a few tape quirks.
ai_review.review: The recording is a high‑quality stereo soundboard mix that delivers the legendary acoustic set in pristine detail, though source 3 shows some harsh oversaturation below ~125 Hz and a couple of mic‑noise blips. Musically the concert shines – “Me & My Uncle”, “Mama Tried”, “Deep Elem Blues” and an electrifying “Speedway Boogie” are repeatedly singled out as highlights, while only a few oddities (a cardboard‑box beat on “Cumberland Blues” and missing bits of “Love Light”) dent an otherwise superb performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews, almost all 4‑5 star, praise both the show (standout acoustic and electric performances) and recording (excellent soundboard with only minor technical flaws).

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stereo soundboard mix praised as crisp and crystal‑clear; occasional oversaturation below ~125 Hz on source 3, mic‑noise on “I Know You Rider”, minor tape‑speed fluctuations and a cardboard‑box beat on one track.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic first set is described as pure gold and uniquely tight; electric second set bristles with virtuosity (notably “Speedway Boogie” and “Hard To Handle”) though a few cuts/odd beats hint at missing material.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work lauded – shredding leads on “Speedway Boogie”, perfect tone on acoustic numbers, occasional electric‑on‑acoustic swaps noted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned for his early rehearsal of “I Know You Rider” and alternate lyrics; no specific performance praise or criticism.
band_member_comments.Keys: NRPS guests (Marmaduke) add high harmonies on acoustic numbers; keyboards not a focus of commentary.
